1. (Currently amended) A method for controlling a flow of air, the method comprising: establishing a level of vacuum in a booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device using a pump; determining whether the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value; __monitoring a pressure differential across the pump__; and terminating the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached the predetermined value __and the pressure differential across the pump exceeds a threshold value__.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein said terminating the flow of air is accomplished via a directional control valve __in response to the monitored pressure differential__, such that a pressure differential across the pump is reduced.

3. (Currently amended) The method of claim 2, wherein said terminating the flow of air includes changing the direction of the flow of air and closing a flow path between the pump and the booster device __based on a control signal responsive to the pressure differential__.

4. (Currently amended) The method of claim 3, wherein said changing the direction of the flow of air includes opening a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump __in a controlled manner to equalize pressures__.

5. (Currently amended) The method of claim 3, wherein said changing the direction of the flow of air includes opening a path for a flow of air between the pump and the atmosphere __through a controlled outlet__.

6. (Currently amended) The method of claim 5, further comprising filtering the flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump via a filter __positioned to remove particulates from the atmospheric air__.

7. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for an automobile braking system __and the pump is driven by an engine control module__.

8. (Currently amended) A system for controlling a flow of air, the system comprising: a booster device configured to provide a vacuum assist when a level of vacuum has been established in the device; a pump configured to establish the level of vacuum in the booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device; __a pressure differential sensor configured to monitor pressure across the pump__; and a directional control valve adapted to terminate the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value __and the pressure differential sensor indicates a threshold pressure differential__, such that a pressure differential across the pump is reduced.

9. (Currently amended) The system of claim 8, wherein the directional control valve is further adapted to change the direction of the flow of air and close a flow path between the pump and the booster device __in response to signals from the pressure differential sensor__.

10. (Currently amended) The system of claim 9, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump __in a metered fashion__.

11. (Currently amended) The system of claim 9, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between the pump and the atmosphere __through a controlled passage__.

12. (Currently amended) The system of claim 11, further comprising a filter adapted for filtering a flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump __to remove contaminants__.

13. (Currently amended) The system of claim 8, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for an automobile braking system __and the pump is operatively controlled by an electronic control unit__.

14. (Currently amended) A motor vehicle comprising: an internal combustion engine; a booster device configured to provide a vacuum assist when a level of vacuum has been established in the device; and a system for controlling a flow of air from the booster device, the system including: a pump configured to establish the level of vacuum in the booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device; __a pressure differential sensor__; and a directional control valve adapted to terminate the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value __and the pressure differential sensor detects a threshold pressure differential__, such that a pressure differential across the pump and a parasitic load on the engine are reduced.

15. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 14, wherein the directional control valve is further adapted to change the direction of the flow of air and close a flow path between the pump and the booster device __responsive to the pressure differential sensor__.

16. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 15, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump __in a regulated manner__.

17. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 15, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between the pump and the atmosphere __through a regulated outlet__.

18. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 17, further comprising a filter adapted for filtering the flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump __to remove airborne particles__.

19. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 14, further comprising a braking system, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for the braking system __and the system includes an electronic control module that controls the directional control valve__.

20. (Currently amended) The vehicle of claim 14, wherein the engine is a compression-ignition type __and the pump is driven by a belt connected to the engine crankshaft__.
